subject: Re: Caching & pricing follow-up: hit rates and effective $/1M tokens

Subject: Post-call recap: caching & pricing assumptions

Ethan / Lydia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from my side and a few asks so we can model an accurate TCO and hit your target unit economics.

Recap:
- Use case: customer support augmentation + personalized product recommendations (mix of short templates + variable user context).
- Rough traffic: you mentioned ~500M tokens/mo as an expected steady-state (with spikes during promos).
- Current cache approach: prefix/template caching for common prompts; no global KV cache in production yet.
- Budget / target: you said $5k–$10k/mo and a target effective rate around $10 / 1M tokens.

Asks / data we need to model pricing accurately:
1) Can you confirm average prompt vs generation split (e.g., avg prompt tokens per request and avg generated tokens)?
2) How often are prompts exact template matches vs lightly parameterized (this drives prefix cache hit rate)?
3) Any retention constraints (how long can entries live in cache)?

Attached: pricing_breakdown.xlsx (preliminary model + assumptions).

Next steps: if you confirm the two points above we can (1) produce a short “effective $/1M tokens” table across hit-rate buckets and (2) propose a 2-week cache experiment to measure an empirical hit rate.

Thanks — I looped Marcus and Aditya on the math side.

—

Thanks Marissa — quick answers below.

Confirmed numbers:
- Expected steady-state: ~500M tokens/month (we saw ~480M in May, expect growth).
- Average prompt tokens: ~80 tokens (system + user prompt + template).
- Average generation: ~220 tokens.
- Template reuse: ~35–45% of requests are exact template matches; another ~20% are lightly parameterized (may get partial prefix reuse).
- Retention: cache entries can be kept for up to 7 days (no legal hold).
- Decision timeline: aiming to pick vendor / commit to an initial pilot by end of month.
- Budget range: $5,000–$10,000 / month target. We’d like an effective $/1M tokens around $10 if possible.

Let me know what you need for the pilot; we can share a small set of logs for a two-week run.

—

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Post-call recap: caching & pricing assumptions (internal calc)

Internal math for Marissa / Aditya — using Ethan’s numbers and our list price assumptions for the model family he’s evaluating.

Assumptions:
- List compute price (hosted API) for target model: $20.00 / 1M tokens (baseline for cost modeling).
- Customer expected volume: 500M tokens/mo.

Effective $/1M calculation: effective_price = list_price * (1 - overall_cache_hit_rate)
(note: this is a simplifying assumption where cache hits avoid model compute cost entirely; real runtime costs for cache reads are negligible vs model inference).

Buckets (examples):
- 0% hit => effective $/1M = $20.00 -> monthly = 500 * $20 = $10,000
- 15% hit (conservative) => effective $/1M = $17.00 -> monthly = 500 * $17 = $8,500
- 40% hit (what Ethan expects if prefix + partial reuse combine) => effective $/1M = $12.00 -> monthly = 500 * $12 = $6,000
- 60% hit (optimistic with aggressive prefix / session caching) => effective $/1M = $8.00 -> monthly = 500 * $8 = $4,000

Notes / nuance:
- Prefix cache vs full-response cache: prefix cache reduces the prompt portion; if only the prompt is cached, the effective savings are proportional to the prompt fraction. With Ethan’s split (~80 prompt / 220 generation = prompt is ~27% of total tokens), a prefix-only cache hit would produce smaller savings unless the prefix is large relative to generation. The numbers above assume an overall hit rate on *total tokens* (i.e., we’re measuring how many tokens are avoided end-to-end).
- Hybrid approach: often we see 2x–3x improvement in effective $/1M vs no-cache for chat-heavy workloads where prompts are templated and responses are short. For FastRetail’s mix, 40% is a reasonable middle estimate.
- Discounting / committed capacity: reserved capacity (Dedicated) can lower list_price materially; we should model a 20–40% committed discount if they commit to a monthly baseline.

Action items I recommend we include in the follow-up to the customer:
1) Run 2-week cache pilot on a representative traffic slice to measure real-world overall_cache_hit_rate and prefix-vs-response split.
2) Produce a landed-cost model that includes reserved-capacity discounts + expected hit-rate buckets.
3) Show a sensitivity table so they can pick a commitment level that hits their $5k–$10k budget.

—
Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Caching & pricing follow-up: hit rates and effective $/1M tokens

Ethan — thanks for the detail, very helpful. Attached is a short PDF (cache-assumptions.pdf) that walks through the same buckets Marcus shared and adds a simple sensitivity matrix with committed-discount examples. High-level summary below and recommended next steps.

Quick summary (based on 500M tokens/mo):
- Baseline (no cache): $20 / 1M => $10,000 / mo
- Conservative (15% hit): $17 / 1M => $8,500 / mo
- Mid (40% hit): $12 / 1M => $6,000 / mo
- Optimistic (60% hit): $8 / 1M => $4,000 / mo

If your target is ~$10 / 1M effective, that maps to an overall hit rate of ~50% against a $20 list price (50% => $10 / 1M -> $5,000 / mo on 500M tokens). There are two levers to get there: (A) improve cache hit rate (prefix + session dedupe + TTL tuning) and (B) take a committed-reserved discount which reduces the list_price term in the equation.

Recommended next steps:
- Pilot: we’ll run a 2-week cache experiment on a subset of traffic (we can give you a small integration guide). We’ll return observed overall_cache_hit_rate and the prompt/generation split. (we’ll need a sample of logs; Marcus, can you share the pilot plan?)
- Pricing model: I’ll share an updated pricing_breakdown.xlsx that includes a 3-tier committed discount scenario and sensitivity to hit rate.
- Meeting: propose 30-min follow-up Thurs 17 Jun to review pilot plan and the landed pricing.

If that works for you Ethan, I’ll send a calendar invite and a small set of steps to export sample logs.

Best —
Marissa Cole
